title: Grand Theft Auto VI released as gamers rejoice globally
summary: After 13 years of waiting, fans around the world will get to play the latest installment in the blockbuster video game series. In focus: A tale of crime and violence in a fictionalized version of…

image.caption: GTA VI is released after more than a decade of developmentImage: Silas Stein/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Grand Theft Auto VI will be officially launched Thursday, ending a 13-year wait for one of the most anticipated games ever.

The game will become playable at midnight local time (CET) on a wide range of platforms, including PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X, meaning gamers in Asia will get to play the game ahead of users in the US and Europe.
In New Zealand, one of the first countries worldwide where the game became available, the release prompted internet providers to prepare for a spike in internet usage at midnight.
This comes due to the game's size of 212 gigabytes, more than a quarter of the average New Zealand household's usage in a month.
Rockstar Games, the company behind the GTA franchise, faces high expectation after 13 years of anticipation, with previous versions having become commercial and cultural hits around the world.
GTA games sold 470 million units worldwide, and the fifth installment generated $1 billion in retail sales in just three days after its release in 2013.

blocks.caption: Jason and Lucia's experiences are at the center of GTA VIImage: Rockstar Games

blocks.text: Take-Two Interactive, Rockstar Games' parent company, saw its shares rise by more than eight percent the day before the game's release.
The game takes place in Vice City, a fictional version of Miami.

It follows Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval, a couple drawn into criminal networks while trying to secure a better life. GTA games are often criticized for including excessive violence and for glorifying crimes and drug use.
Lucia, a former prisoner, and Jason, an ex-military man, experience a series of criminal jobs that go wrong in the drug-trafficking world of Leonida, a fictional state based on Florida.
According to Rockstar, Leonida is the company's most detailed open world so far, extending beyond Vice City into smaller communities and nightlife hotspots inspired by locations in South Florida.
Music has been an intrinsic part of the GTA experience, and the latest game is expected to feature a soundtrack including artists like Tame Impala and SZA.
